newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai soybeans end mixed in slow trading.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai soybeans end mixed in slow trading.

text.p: Shanghai soybean futures ended mixed in slow trading on Wednesday on continued uncertainty over the short-term market trend, traders said.
The key January 1997 contract ended at an intra-day high of 3,210 yuan ($387) per tonne, down 20 yuan. It opened at a low of 3,190.
March rose 50 to 3,250, May fell 52 to 3,298, July rose two to 3,362, September rose nine to 3,379 and November was unchanged at 3,400.
Combined volume fell to 12,000 tonnes from 14,900.
Traders said few investors were interested in trading soybeans due to a lack of market-moving news.
"Many investors have moved their money into more active markets, including Shanghai's stock market," one trader said.
"Soybeans are likely to continue to move around 3,200 yuan in the next few days," he added.
Traders said fundamentals had changed little, with the result that futures prices will move in a narrow range in the short term. ($1=8.3009)
